events.text: Case opened: The Nightingale Vanishes

On Thursday at 21:40, insurance appraiser Odile Marchetti examined the Ravel Gallery's prize piece — the Nightingale, a nineteenth-century jewelled clockwork bird insured for 3.5 million — in the gallery's vault and declared it a replica. The real bird is gone. The vault was locked all week and nobody reported a break-in. In the previous ten days the bird had been out for restoration and returned on Monday night; the vault was also opened in the small hours of Wednesday. Gallery owner Lucien Ravel recently raised the insurance cover. Restorer Irene Vance had the bird in her studio. Security consultant Felix Dorn built the vault system. Find out when the switch happened, who made it, and whether anyone should be charged.
Set out how I intend to run this.

The Nightingale went into a locked vault on Monday night and came out a fake on Thursday. I want that window accounted for by records before I listen to anyone's version of it: doors, cameras, the scene itself. Lucien Ravel, Irene Vance, Felix Dorn — three people with a quarrel is three stories to test, not three suspects. Nobody is the answer yet.
Flag the easy assumption.
Nobody broke in, so the records will tell us more than the lock. I want the vault log, the camera files, and the replica itself, sealed and logged. I'll report what they show and nothing more.
Tell the team what a charge needs.

For a charge I need three things pointing at one person: a motive, the opportunity, and something physical that ties them to the vault and the display case. A quarrel is not a case. And if you go into anyone's private space, you bring me a warrant first — I will not lose an exhibit to a suppression motion.

events.text: Name every doubt the record supports.

Members of the jury, the question is not whether Irene Vance could have done this. It is whether the prosecution has made you sure. The vault corridor CCTV: the Wednesday figure's face is never visible. The restoration work order: a restorer handling the object is exactly what she was hired to do. The freight manifest: the crate was never opened or inspected. The night guard's logbook: the Wednesday rounds were filled in afterwards in a single sitting. Each of those gaps is a reasonable doubt, and the law says what you do with a reasonable doubt. Not guilty.

events.text: Irene Vance switched the Nightingale on Monday night, not Wednesday. Insolvent and owed two years of fees by Lucien Ravel, she spent the ten days of the restoration casting a replica from a silicone mould. On Monday she asked the night guard to pause the corridor camera 'for her photographs', put the fake in the display case at 23:09, and walked out of the loading door with the real bird in her equipment case. On Tuesday morning she shipped it to a dealer in Antwerp as 'restoration materials' declared at 900,000. The vault opening on Wednesday night that looked like the theft was Felix Dorn secretly replacing a faulty sensor; the owner with the debts and the raised insurance was at a card table across town.

detective.name: Inspector Sol Reyes
detective.tagline: Follows the timeline until it confesses.
detective.personality: Methodical, patient, allergic to assumptions. Builds a timeline first and distrusts any theory that arrives too early.
detective.background: Twenty years in major crimes. Lost a case once by charging the obvious man.

forensic.name: Dr. Chidi Okonkwo
forensic.tagline: The evidence says what it says, and no more.
forensic.personality: Dry, exact, refuses to overstate a finding. Volunteers limitations before anyone asks.
forensic.background: Trace-evidence specialist. Has testified four hundred times and been wrong, to his knowledge, once.

prosecutor.name: ADA Vivian Calloway
prosecutor.tagline: Charges what she can prove, and proves it.
prosecutor.personality: Disciplined and economical. Builds on admitted exhibits only; drops a weak point rather than defend it.
prosecutor.background: Fifteen years of homicide trials. Has never been reversed on appeal.

defense.personality: Forensic in cross-examination. Attacks the weakest link in each exhibit and never asks a question she cannot use.
